topics.title: Curvature
topics.description: Understand how quickly a curve changes direction, from intuition to radius-of-curvature formulas.

blocks.title: What is curvature?
paragraphs: Curvature describes how quickly the direction of a moving point on a curve changes as the point travels along the curve.
A straight line has zero curvature because its direction does not change. A tightly bending curve has larger curvature.

steps.title: Move along the curve
steps.text: Imagine a tiny arrow tangent to the curve. As the point moves, watch the arrow rotate.

steps.title: Measure the turning
steps.text: Compare the small change in tangent direction with the small distance travelled along the curve.

steps.title: Define curvature
steps.text: The ratio of turning angle to arc length approaches the curvature when the interval becomes extremely small.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: Curvature is about change of direction, not simply how high or low the graph is.

topics.title: Expected Value
topics.description: Build the idea of E(X) from weighted outcomes, then connect it to variance and E(X²).

blocks.title: The central idea
paragraphs: Expected value is the probability-weighted average of the possible values of a random variable.
It is not necessarily a value that the random variable can actually take. It represents the long-run average outcome of repeated trials.

blocks.title: Discrete expected value
blocks.explanation: Multiply each possible outcome by its probability and add the results.

blocks.explanation: This identity connects the second moment E(X²) with the square of the mean.

blocks.title: Quick check
blocks.question: A fair die has outcomes 1,2,3,4,5,6. Find E(X).

topics.title: Newton’s Laws
topics.description: See force, mass and acceleration as one connected model rather than three isolated statements.

steps.title: No net force
steps.text: If the net external force is zero, velocity remains constant.

steps.title: Apply a net force
steps.text: A non-zero net force changes velocity, producing acceleration.

steps.title: Change the mass
steps.text: For the same net force, greater mass means smaller acceleration.

blocks.title: Second law
blocks.explanation: Acceleration points in the direction of the net force and its magnitude is proportional to net force and inversely related to mass.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Do not use one individual force in F = ma when several forces act. Use the vector sum, the net force.

topics.title: Demand & Value
topics.description: Explore why people buy, what shifts demand and how markets translate needs into prices.

blocks.title: What demand means
paragraphs: Demand is the quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing and able to buy at different prices during a given period.
A change in the good's own price generally causes movement along the demand curve. Changes in income, tastes, expectations and prices of related goods can shift the curve.

blocks.title: Demand is not just desire
blocks.text: A person may want a product without having the willingness and ability to purchase it. Effective demand combines desire with purchasing power and willingness.

blocks.title: Quick check
blocks.question: If the price of a product rises and everything else stays constant, what usually happens to quantity demanded?
blocks.hint: Think about movement along the same demand curve.
blocks.solution: Quantity demanded generally falls, assuming the ordinary downward-sloping demand relationship.

topics.title: APIs Explained
topics.description: A visual guide to requests, responses, endpoints, authentication and real application data flows.

steps.title: Client
steps.text: A browser or app sends a request to a server endpoint.

steps.title: Server
steps.text: The server validates the request, runs application logic and accesses data when needed.

steps.title: Response
steps.text: The server sends structured data, often JSON, back to the client.

blocks.title: Production rule
blocks.text: Never put private API keys or secrets directly in frontend JavaScript. Public clients can be inspected by anyone.

blocks.title: Typical API shape
blocks.formula: Client → HTTPS request → API → data/service → JSON response
blocks.explanation: The exact architecture varies, but this is a useful mental model for modern web applications.

topics.title: AP & GP Summation
topics.description: Turn arithmetic and geometric series into patterns you can see, derive and remember.

blocks.title: Sequence versus series
paragraphs: A sequence is an ordered list of terms. A series is the sum of terms from a sequence.
Arithmetic progressions change by a constant difference. Geometric progressions multiply by a constant ratio.

blocks.title: Arithmetic progression
blocks.explanation: a is the first term, d is the common difference and n is the number of terms.

blocks.title: Geometric progression
blocks.explanation: a is the first term and r is the common ratio.

blocks.title: Quick check
blocks.question: Find the sum of 2 + 5 + 8 + 11 + 14.
blocks.hint: Identify a, d and n, then use the AP sum formula.
